shared_context.topic: flu test and influenza test terminology

atoms.1: The terms 'flu test' and 'influenza test' are often used interchangeably.
atoms.2: Flu test and influenza test refer to diagnostic tests used to detect the presence of the influenza virus in a patient's body.
atoms.3: Influenza tests typically involve collecting a sample from the nose, throat, or other respiratory areas.
atoms.4: Influenza tests typically involve sending the collected sample to a laboratory for analysis.
atoms.5: The specific terms 'flu test' and 'influenza test' may vary depending on the context and location.
atoms.6: The terms 'flu test' and 'influenza test' generally refer to the same concept.
atoms.7: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) uses the term 'influenza diagnostic tests.'
atoms.8: The CDC includes rapid influenza diagnostic tests (RIDTs) under influenza diagnostic tests.
atoms.9: The CDC includes molecular assays like PCR (polymerase chain reaction) under influenza diagnostic tests.
atoms.10: Rapid influenza diagnostic tests (RIDTs) provide quick results, usually within 15-30 minutes.
atoms.11: Rapid influenza diagnostic tests (RIDTs) are often used in outpatient settings.
atoms.12: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tests are molecular tests.
atoms.13: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tests detect the genetic material of the influenza virus.
atoms.14: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tests are often used in clinical laboratories.
atoms.15: Immunochromatographic tests use antibodies to detect the presence of influenza antigens in a sample.
atoms.16: Immunochromatographic tests are often used in point-of-care settings.
atoms.17: Flu test and influenza test refer to the same type of diagnostic test used to detect the presence of the influenza virus.

snippets.output: The terms “flu test” and “influenza test” are often used interchangeably.
Flu test and influenza test refer to diagnostic tests used to detect the presence of the influenza virus in the body.
Influenza tests typically involve collecting a sample from the nose, throat, or other respiratory areas and sending the collected sample to a laboratory for analysis.
The specific terms “flu test” and “influenza test” may vary depending on the context and location.
The terms “flu test” and “influenza test” generally refer to the same concept.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) uses the term “influenza diagnostic tests,” which includes rapid influenza diagnostic tests (RIDTs) and molecular assays such as PCR (polymerase chain reaction).
Rapid influenza diagnostic tests (RIDTs) are often used in outpatient settings and provide quick results, usually within 15–30 minutes.
Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tests are molecular tests that detect the genetic material of the influenza virus and are often used in clinical laboratories.
Immunochromatographic tests use antibodies to detect the presence of influenza antigens in a sample and are often used in point-of-care settings.
Flu test and influenza test refer to the same type of diagnostic test used to detect the presence of the influenza virus.
